direction.premise: A shared picture puzzle turns each drag path into a temporary obstacle for the other mosaic builders.
direction.composition: An immersive restoration workbench: brass-framed luminous mosaic surface is the protagonist; compact archival HUD above and a shallow personal material tray below. On desktop, tray becomes a side rail.
direction.shapeLanguage: Precision squared ceramic-like tiles, thin seams, brass rivets, editorial rectangular workshop controls and sweeping continuous ribbon paths.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Mineral graphite workshop surrounds a matte ivory underlay and inset antique brass frame. Picture fragments retain original SVG artworks and acquire small edges, lift shadows and careful magnetic seating.
direction.paletteLogic: Warm ivory, graphite, aged copper and restrained pigment for the furniture. Player-specific path colors remain true to server palette to preserve path ownership.
direction.typography: Humanist interface combined with Georgia editorial exhibit headlines and technical monospaced micro-labels. Timer and score remain operational, not decorative.
direction.signature: A tile lifts above the finger and is guided around fading pigment ribbons on a shared lit conservation surface; a completed picture is unveiled as an archive exhibit.
direction.distinction: Unlike Zamazka's painted restoration, Trace Mosaic has physically located fragments and non-overlapping player-owned route paths. Unlike Perekos there is no arena/character UI.

architecture.primaryVerb: Drag only your assigned picture fragments to their correct cells while choosing routes around other players’ fading trails.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Offset lifted fragment, target-cell state, visible real trail geometry, snap-in arrival, optional haptic and subdued audio.
architecture.spatialRationale: A square picture grid stays above a compact tray of the viewer’s assigned fragments; room, time and completion sit in a single top row. This keeps the current game object and its real inputs spatially connected on a phone.

production.renderer: Persistent DOM mosaic tiles, absolute SVG path overlay and CSS physical-material treatment. Network snapshots patch pieces/trays instead of rebuilding the input surface.
production.focalAsset: The authored source SVG puzzle catalog and a bespoke inset-workbench app icon; no downloaded stock assets.

motion.character: Subtle lifted ghost follows the pointer; a selected target glows, denied target is striped and a correct piece seats with an overshoot.
motion.action: Carry personal fragments across the board without crossing 30-second peer ribbons.
motion.anticipation: Personal tile lifts with directional offset above touch, enabling precision drop.
motion.response: Authoritative result drives on-board placement, quiet audio and haptic success.
motion.followThrough: Correctly placed tile remains visible with a short settling motion; server trails age visibly.
motion.interruption: Repeated input uses the current state; pointer cancellation releases held controls and hidden tabs stop transmitting held actions.
motion.reducedMotion: CSS animation and transitions are disabled through prefers-reduced-motion while trails and placement states remain legible.

evidence.expectedChange: An offline solo puzzle lobby opens; starting it assigns every fragment to the local builder.
